question: Does the current context-signature alias substrate preserve abstraction when alias pairs have identical raw context support but slightly different context frequencies?
hypothesis: The existing exact-equality context-signature inducer will pass the unchanged exact-context positive control, but a bounded 9/7/8/8 versus 8/8/8/8 frequency jitter across the same four context keys will split all nine semantic alias pairs into eighteen singleton classes. If so, count-jitter robustness is falsified even though every true alias pair retains context-support Jaccard 1.0 and total-variation distance only 0.03125.

prior_evidence.observation: Context-induced aliases achieved 1.0 accuracy across all 192 unseen mixed-alias multi-step programs; exact-surface scored 0.026041666666666668 and shuffled-context 0.14583333333333334.

scope_statement: This falsifies only robustness of exact context-count signature equality to small frequency drift. It does not invalidate the prior exact-context abstraction or reasoning results.
authority: research-only; no deployment, external-model inference, scheduler, queue, accepted-ref, production, broker, or live-interface authority

surface_representation.selection: top eighteen raw four-byte windows by occurrence count descending then lexicographic key

jitter_bridge.context_keys: identical four raw immediate-context keys to the positive control for each semantic entity

induction.signature: complete sorted exact context-key -> count map

validity_criteria: Exact parent and North Star identities match.
Surface representations are selected from the unchanged task corpus before either bridge is evaluated.
Positive-control and jitter bridges use identical context-key identities for each semantic entity; only family-1 frequencies differ.
Every jitter alias still has exactly 32 bridge observations.
Support Jaccard and total-variation metrics are computed from observed raw bridge context counts, not construction labels.
Semantic/family mappings are evaluator-only after induction for pair diagnostics.
Full Go regression passes before the probe and all metrics are finite.
No tokenizer, external model, network call, alias dictionary, capacity growth, adaptive clustering, or post-result tuning occurs.

classification_rules.survives_falsification: Validity passes, normal control passes, and jitter_correct_evaluator_alias_pair_count remains 9 with nine two-member classes.
classification_rules.count_jitter_robustness_falsified: Validity passes, normal control passes, support Jaccard is 1.0, total variation is 0.03125, and jitter_correct_evaluator_alias_pair_count is 0 with eighteen classes.
classification_rules.mixed: Validity passes but jitter behavior falls between those criteria.
classification_rules.incomplete: Compute interruption prevents both frozen bridge evaluations.
classification_rules.invalid: Any context-support identity, observation cardinality, evaluator boundary, representation, or qualification criterion fails.

no_post_result_tuning_rule: No bridge frequency, context key, representation rule, signature rule, metric, threshold, or interpretation may change after primary output.
